Kong, L., Hasanbeigi, A., Price, L., 2016. Assessment of emerging energy-efficiency technologies for the pulp and paper industry: a technical review. Journal of Cleaner Production 122, 5-28. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jclepro.2015.12.116

Review of 25 emerging technologies. Loaded: a description and state-of-development row for each technology (plus comparators: steam-heated cylinder dryer, conventional recovery system; black liquor gasification split into BLG and BLGCC; biomass gasification into power and steam; Condebelt into new and retrofit; the 7 EBTP biorefinery chains of Table 7 as separate technologies); capex where printed (microwave pre-treatment, surfactant spray cell, high-consistency former, impulse drying, Condebelt new/retrofit, BLG, BLGCC, conventional recovery, biorefinery first-commercial plants); gas-fired vs steam dryer efficiency; levelized electricity and steam cost from biomass gasification; LignoBoost demo capacity; a few temperatures/pressures. NOT loaded in the main file: energy savings, which the paper gives only relative to conventional practice (%, GJ/t or kWh/t saved) - these are in _measures.csv; no absolute specific energy consumption is printed for any technology. Payback periods, cost savings and demonstration-plant costs are in _measures.csv / _other-values.csv. No TRL loaded: the paper's maturity categories are explicitly not TRLs (p.7). No flows file (no per-unit flows printed).

1. No currency year is given for any cost; most costs are reprinted from older studies (Martin et al. 2000a/b, Larson et al. 2003/2009, Bain et al. 2003, Deng and Zhu 2004, EBTP 2011), so price years span roughly 2000-2011; currency units carry no year. 2. Capital cost bases are rarely stated (equipment vs installed vs total plant); plant capacities for BLG, conventional recovery and biorefinery costs are not printed. 3. '$/t paper' capex figures do not say whether they are per tonne of annual capacity. 4. Microwave pre-treatment cost is for a '1000 Adt mill' without a time base. 5. BLGCC capex range differs between Table 6 ($200-400 million) and text ($200-500 million for all configurations). 6. Enzymatic pre-treatment savings differ between Table 2 (pectinase up to 20%, xylanase up to 26%) and text (10%, 25%). 7. Condebelt steam saving given as 15% in text and 10-20% in Table 5. 8. Duplicated sentence on oxalic acid bleaching chemicals (p.8). 9. Gas-fired dryer efficiency (75-80% vs 65%) basis undefined. 10. Maturity categories are the authors' own and are not TRLs.
